questions.question: A first-grade teacher says the word “map” aloud and asks students to say the word again without the /m/ sound. Which foundational reading skill is the teacher assessing?
questions.explanation: Removing /m/ from “map” requires a student to delete one phoneme and identify the remaining sounds. Syllable blending combines larger spoken units rather than removing an individual sound.

questions.question: A student claims that 3/8 is greater than 1/2 because 3 is greater than 1. Which representation would best help the student correct this misconception?
options: Place both fractions on the same number line from 0 to 1
List the first eight multiples of 3
Rewrite both fractions as mixed numbers
Compare only the denominators of the fractions
questions.explanation: A common number line makes the fractions’ magnitudes directly comparable and shows 3/8 to the left of 1/2. Comparing isolated numerators or denominators does not account for the size of the fractional parts.
